title: App launch time
summary: Launch = the system loading your app, your setup code, and the first frame. Make it fast by doing only what the first screen needs and deferring the rest.
body: **In simple words:** Users judge your app in the first second. Launch time is everything from tapping the icon to the first usable screen.
**Types:** **Cold** launch - app not in memory (after reboot or long time). **Warm** - parts still cached. **Resume** - app was in background; not a real launch.

**Phases:** (1) Pre-main: the system loads your binary and dynamic frameworks (dyld), fixes up pointers, runs static initializers. (2) `main` → `UIApplicationMain` → app delegate `didFinishLaunching`. (3) First frame rendered.

**Making it faster:** fewer dynamic frameworks (prefer static linking or mergeable libraries); no heavy `+load` or static initializers; in `didFinishLaunching` do only what the first screen needs; delay analytics/ads SDK setup; no synchronous network, big disk reads or Keychain reads on main; show cached content immediately instead of a spinner.
**Measure:** Instruments App Launch template, `XCTApplicationLaunchMetric` in performance tests, Xcode Organizer launch time (real users, p50/p90), MetricKit.
**Staff angle:** set a launch budget, add a CI performance test that fails on regressions, attribute startup cost per module/SDK, and make teams own their part.
keyPoints: Cold vs warm vs resume; Apple recommends first frame within ~400 ms.
Pre-main cost: dynamic frameworks and static initializers.
Post-main: do the minimum in `didFinishLaunching`; defer SDKs; lazy-load features.
Measure in lab (Instruments, XCTest) and field (Organizer, MetricKit) and guard in CI.
mistakes: Measuring only on a new iPhone in debug mode; measure release builds on older devices.
followups: **What is the watchdog (`0x8badf00d`)?** The system kills apps that block the main thread too long during launch or resume.
**What is prewarming?** iOS may start your process before the user taps; do not assume `didFinishLaunching` time equals user-visible time.
